# Current best local solution, explained (2026-10-10) Scope: what the best local-validation model is, how the data become predictions, how it is trained and distilled, what HPO does, and what the numbers do and do not support. Everything cited is a file in this repository; plots are generated by [`scripts/make_solution_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/make_solution_report.py) and [`scripts/extract_train_loss.py`](../../../../../scripts/extract_train_loss.py) from saved predictions, logs and ledgers (nothing is redrawn by hand). **One-sentence summary.** A 2-layer GRU (width 256, no attention) over 211 per-row inputs is first trained from scratch as a *teacher* (Muon on the recurrent matrices, one-cycle schedule, weighted-MSE on the official metric weights), then a *student* with the same architecture is warm-started from a teacher and fine-tuned for 3 epochs on a blend of the true labels (30%) and the averaged predictions of four teacher families (70%). The student is what is served (one core, about 74 µs/row in the native int16 kernel). --- ## 1. Data and what the 112 columns are * Each sequence is 20,000 rows × 112 anonymous float columns; two targets (t0, t1) per row; the metric is scored only on rows ≥ 99 and where the official mask is true. Data: `datasets/train.parquet` (about 10.6k sequences), `datasets/valid.parquet` (1,873 sequences, 4 component-disjoint folds, fold 1 = 457 evaluation sequences in 149 components (older notes say 468)). Sequences are consecutive 20k-row chunks of 3,288 continuous streams ([findings](../../../../../research/findings-2026-09-26.md)). * The column layout is an **order book of two instruments** ([`src/wnn/data.py`](../../../../../src/wnn/data.py)): per instrument 11 bid prices, 11 ask prices, 11 bid volumes, 11 ask volumes, 4 trade prices, 4 trade volumes (52 columns; instruments at offsets 0 and 52) plus 8 extra columns (104-111). Prices and volumes are quantile-transformed; many columns are held constant between updates (multi-rate clocks: blocks update on 12%, 15%, 31%, 40%, 70% or 100% of rows). * Targets are trade PnLs against a common future price F: `t0 = F - ask`, `t1 = bid - F`; the label is piecewise constant in time (mean run 9.5 rows) and defined by the **future** book. A teacher that may see future rows scores far higher (section 9). * Metric `global_wp_clip2_v1` ([`src/wnn/gmetric.py`](../../../../../src/wnn/gmetric.py)): Pearson pooled over rows and both targets with weights |clip(y, 2)|, both prediction and target clipped to ±2. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[20,000 x 112 raw columns
2 order books + 8 extra] --> B[event features
99 per row] A --> C[raw 112] B --> D[concat: 211 inputs] C --> D D --> E[z-score with fit-set mean/std
folded into the first layer at export] E --> F[Linear 211 to 256 + GELU] F --> G[2-layer GRU, h=256, zero initial state] G --> H[head: concat GRU out + encoder skip
Linear 512 to 256, GELU, Linear 256 to 2] H --> I[t0, t1 prediction per row] ``` ### Event features (99 per row; [`src/wnn/features.py`](../../../../../src/wnn/features.py)) First differences of the instrument-0 price block, instrument-0 volume block and instrument-1 price block (22 + 22 + 22), eight event flags (price move, bid/ask volume change, trade price/volume, instrument-1 price/volume/trade), three "rows since last event" counters, and the last non-zero price difference (22). They are computed causally inside the trainer (`event_features_torch`) and by the native engine at serving. Inputs total 112 + 99 = **211** (the `normalization_identity` shape in every `history.json`). ## 2. Architecture (and the attention question) * **No attention in the best model.** Source: [`RNNModel` in `src/wnn/nn.py`](../../../../../research/campaign_2026-10-06/bandit_continuation/continuous_execution_E529/h230_source_v6_lead/src/wnn/nn.py) with `enc=linear`. A token-attention encoder (`enc=tokens`, PyTorch `nn.TransformerEncoderLayer`, per-block tokens with a CLS token) and a causal conv encoder exist as research options; they are not in the served model (the native engine supports the linear encoder only) and did not help. * **Encoder:** `Linear(211 -> 256)` then GELU (`z`). Input normalisation uses a fit-set mean/std buffer; at export the normalisation is folded into this layer so zero raw inputs can be skipped column by column. * **Recurrent core:** PyTorch `nn.GRU(256, 256, num_layers=2, batch_first=True)` (cuDNN fused). **State:** the initial hidden state is zero (`h=None`); it is reset at the start of every sequence; during training a sequence is processed in chunks of 1000-2000 rows with the state carried from chunk to chunk and **detached** (truncated BPTT), so gradients reach back one chunk only. At serving the native engine carries the state row by row and resets it at the sequence boundary. * **Head:** `[GRU output ; encoder output z] -> Linear(512,256) -> GELU -> Linear(256, n_out)`. `n_out` is 2 plus training-only auxiliary columns (structure head, next-change head, and for students a four-family head); only the first two outputs are served. * **Size:** about 1.04 M parameters at width 256 (log line `params 1.04M`). Width 384 is about 2.2× the cost per row and is not servable on the current kernel (733 µs/row vs 74 µs/row). ## 3. Teacher training (from scratch) Recipe of the default "scratch teacher" (`DEFAULTS` in [`hpo/space.py`](../../../../../hpo/space.py), a launched command in [`local_queue_r1/done/66_f0ep3s5-fit.json`](../local_queue_r1/done/66_f0ep3s5-fit.json)): | Item | Value | |---|---| | Optimizer | **Muon on the GRU weight matrices** (`weight_ih`, `weight_hh`; Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation, 5 steps, bf16; scope `rnn`) and **AdamW** for the input layer, head and biases (`MuonAdamW` in `src/wnn/optim.py`); lr 1e-3, weight decay 0.01, Muon lr multiplier 1 | | Schedule | OneCycle, 5% warm-up to the max lr, cosine decay to max_lr/(25·100) ([plot](plots/lr_schedules.png)); 3-4 epochs | | Batch | 32 sequences per step, chunk 1000 rows (20 optimizer steps per sequence), 373 batches and 7,460 optimizer steps per epoch (11,949 sampled sequences), fp16 autocast with GradScaler (about 5 skipped updates per epoch) | | Loss | weighted MSE on `y` clipped to ±2 with weights |clip(y,2)| (`--loss wmse`, chunk-normalised), the same weights as the metric; plus auxiliary structure (0.3) and next-change (0.3) heads | | Row weighting | `--propensity`, `--valid-true-mask`: the official scored mask is only known for valid sequences, so training rows are weighted by an estimated probability of being scored (power 2, floor 0.03) and valid sequences use the true mask | | Time | about 560-620 s per epoch on the local GPU, about 45 min for 3 epochs | ![learning rate](plots/lr_schedules.png) **What the logs and checkpoints keep.** Every run directory in `artifacts/runs//` (9.3 GB total) holds `model_ep{E}.pt` per epoch, `model.pt`, `training_state.pt`, `history.json` (per-epoch seconds, optimizer attempts/skipped steps, sample-order and normalisation hashes) and `provenance.json` (source and split hashes). **Validation is deliberately not computed during fitting** (`--no-eval-during-fit`: campaign rule), so `history.json` says `evaluation: withheld`; the learning curve is rebuilt afterwards from saved snapshots with [`scripts/snapshot_curve.py`](../../../../../scripts/snapshot_curve.py) ([plot](plots/learning_curves.png)). Training loss lives only in the text logs (`runtime/logs/*.log`, one line per 20 batches); until now it was not structured, so [`scripts/extract_train_loss.py`](../../../../../scripts/extract_train_loss.py) now parses it to CSV ([`train_loss_csv/`](train_loss_csv/), [plot](plots/train_loss.png)). Gap I recommend closing: persist the train loss in `history.json` per epoch. ![learning curves](plots/learning_curves.png) ![train loss](plots/train_loss.png) Reading the curves: on fold 1 the default run reaches 0.666 by epoch 2-3; the 6-epoch run peaks at 0.6671 at the end of epoch 3 and then drops (0.662, 0.649), i.e. memorisation, not under-training. Mid-epoch snapshots are as good as epoch ends. ## 4. Student and distillation (the top local model) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph T[Four teacher families on the same fold, all independently trained] T1[strong: combo scratch s3, s4
coef 0.15 each] T2[full_finetuned: since-weight finetunes
coef 0.10 each] T3[raw_wmse: since s3, s4
coef 0.125 each] T4[samefold baseline: two width-384 raw-wmse runs
coef 0.03125 each] end T --> CACHE[(distillation cache: per-row predictions of every family
cache/h230_four_family_fold1_source_20261009_r1
sum of coefficients 0.8125)] CACHE --> BLEND[target = 0.3 x true label + 0.7 x blended teacher] P[parent: c20261003_combo_s3_f1 epoch 3
warm start of the student] --> S BLEND --> S[student: same 2x256 GRU
AdamW lr 1e-4, one-cycle, 3 epochs, batch 16
+ family head weight 0.1] S --> OUT[served: first 2 outputs] ``` * Recipe (launch file: [`done/72_h230-f1-s3-ep3-chunk1000-fit-r1.json`](../local_queue_r1/done/72_h230-f1-s3-ep3-chunk1000-fit-r1.json); the best student `h230_f1_s3_ep3` uses chunk 2000): `--init c20261003_combo_s3_f1@ep3`, `--distill-alpha 0.7`, `--distill-family-head --distill-family-weight 0.1 --distill-family-target-mode raw`, `--optim adamw --lr 1e-4 --sched onecycle --epochs 3 --batch 16`, no bootstrap substitution (`--distill-boot-h 0`). * Why it works at all: the student is a *warm-started* copy of a good scratch teacher, then pulled toward the average of several differently trained teachers (their errors are only partly shared: pairwise correlation 0.95-0.99). It gains about +0.003 over a scratch teacher; the gain comes from the chain (parent + blended targets), not from the student knob settings (twelve variants span 0.0010, see [LOOP_LOG](../LOOP_LOG_20261010.md), student-stage evidence entry). Distilling wider (384) or ensemble teachers into the 256 student did **not** transfer. * Files: cache builder [`scripts/build_distill_cache.py`](../../../../../scripts/build_distill_cache.py), pipeline [`scripts/distill_pipeline.py`](../../../../../scripts/distill_pipeline.py), cache metadata [`metadata.json`](../../../../../cache/h230_four_family_fold1_source_20261009_r1/metadata.json). ## 5. Validation: how scores are produced and how far to trust them * **Folds:** 4 component-disjoint folds of the 1,873 valid sequences (a component = a chain of consecutive chunks of one stream, so no neighbour leaks). A fold-k run trains on `train` plus the valid sequences of the other folds and evaluates on fold k only ([`splits/fold1.json`](../../../../../research/campaign_2026-09-29/artifacts/splits/fold1.json)). Fold levels differ: about 0.668 / 0.679 / 0.703 / 0.707. * **Noise (measured, [`hpo/VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md`](../../../../../hpo/VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md)):** seed-to-seed sd 0.0010; evaluation-unit noise of a paired difference sd 0.0018; one-run one-fold A/B comparison sd about 0.0022 (95% ±0.0043). Hardware drift about 0.0002. * **Tiers:** T0 screen (fold 1, 1 run: kills disasters only), T1 dev (folds 1 and 0, fold-difficulty adjusted), T2 confirm (folds 2 and 3 reserved, one evaluation per finalist), T3 train-holdout veto, T4 public (lineage level only). ## 6. HPO: what it is, what it tunes, how it is validated * **Yes, hyper-parameter optimisation:** Optuna TPE with durable SQLite + event log ([`hpo/studies/teacher_v2/`](../../../../../hpo/studies/teacher_v2/), code in [`hpo/`](../../../../../hpo/)), a MedianPruner, ask/tell over Vast lane B, a duplicate-proposal guard and per-tick seeding. * **Parameters (space v2, [`hpo/space.py`](../../../../../hpo/space.py)):** optimizer (`muon_rnn` / `muon_hidden`), lr 6e-4..2e-3, Muon multiplier 0.5..2, weight decay 3e-3..6e-2, schedule (`onecycle`, `wsd_sqrt`, `wsd_linear`, `sgdr`) with its conditional knobs, epochs {2,3,4,5}, width {256,320,384}, layers {2,3}, RNN init (`default`, `chrono`, `orth`, `chrono_orth`), loss (`wmse`, `wmse_gcorr`, `mix`), class-3 weight 0.7..2.5, weight averaging (none/EMA/SWA), dropout 0..0.25. Seeds are never searched. * **Validation inside HPO:** each trial runs on dev fold 1, then fold 0; the objective is the mean of the two with fold 0 reduced by the fold-difficulty offset (prior 0.0131, re-estimated from trials that have both). Pruning compares after fold 1. Folds 2 and 3 are **never** used for search; `orchestrator confirm` runs the top finalists once on them (pre-registered rule: confirm if mean delta ≥ 0 and class-3 delta ≥ 0). * **State today (56 asked, 50 told: 18 complete, 28 pruned, 4 failed):** best by objective: trial 35 (0.66876: muon_hidden, lr 1e-3, WSD-linear, h384, dropout 0.16, SWA), 27 (0.66779, 3 layers, wmse_gcorr, class-3 weight 2.45), 46, 41, 13. T2: trial 2 (h384) 0.70737 on fold 3; trial 27 0.70249 on fold 2. ![HPO](plots/hpo_fold_scatter.png) ### The "delta +0.002" evidence ([`hpo/evidence/scratch_effects_fold1.json`](../../../../../hpo/evidence/scratch_effects_fold1.json), [`scripts/evidence_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/evidence_report.py)) It compares 47 scratch models on fold 1 against the mean of four default-recipe runs (0.66642, seed sd 0.00106). The largest raw deltas are +0.0028 (h384 with dropout 0.2), +0.0022 (gated), +0.0017 (h384 fixed-mix), +0.0016 (h384). **All 95% intervals cover zero** (about ±0.005: component bootstrap and seed noise in quadrature), and after empirical-Bayes shrinkage (true-effect sd 0.0015 vs measurement sd 0.0024) they are +0.0003..+0.0006. They are therefore *hypotheses*, not findings. ![forest](plots/evidence_forest.png) How we use it: (1) it set the decision thresholds and narrowed the HPO space (epochs ≤ 5, no corr/Huber/TCN, width ≤ 384); (2) the consistent sign of width 384 across **four** folds (mean +0.0012) is the only lever that survived; (3) the high-raw-delta variants (h384+dropout, gated) are the candidates worth a confirmation on reserved folds 2/3 and a place in a *diverse* ensemble, not a ranking claim; (4) it fixes how many runs a claim needs (about 4 folds × 3 seeds per arm for ±0.002). ## 7. Local validation: which result is the best example Fold 1 (457 evaluation sequences, 149 components; bootstrap over components, 1000 draws; paired intervals against the matched control `r3_ctrl_f1_s3_e3`, produced by [`make_solution_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/make_solution_report.py), table in [`fold1_ci.json`](fold1_ci.json)): | Model | Fold-1 WP | 95% CI (unpaired) | Δ vs control s3 | 95% CI of Δ (paired) | |---|---|---|---|---| | student: distilled from h256 scratch teachers (`vt_f1_dsq_t256`) | 0.66938 | [0.6229, 0.7127] | +0.0033 | [+0.0011, +0.0059] | | **student: H230 ep3, four teacher families (`h230_f1_s3_ep3`)** | **0.66922** | [0.6220, 0.7125] | **+0.0032** | **[+0.0016, +0.0049]** | | teacher: scratch h384 chunk500 3 ep | 0.66900 | [0.6217, 0.7113] | +0.0029 | [+0.0004, +0.0057] | | student ep3 + bootstrap 8 | 0.66821 | [0.6215, 0.7119] | +0.0022 | [+0.0004, +0.0041] | | teacher: scratch default (v6 trainer) s3 / s4 | 0.66606 / 0.66582 | | 0 / -0.0002 | [-0.0022, +0.0015] | ![fold 1 CI](plots/fold1_ci.png) **Best example to explain: `h230_f1_s3_ep3`** (fold-1 WP 0.66922). It is the only model whose paired improvement over the control is large relative to its interval (+0.0032, lower bound +0.0016) and it has the cleanest provenance (one declared parent, four independently trained teacher families, fixed coefficients). The unpaired intervals (±0.045) are wide because sequences differ hugely in difficulty; paired differences are what matter. Caveats: this is one seed and one fold, the paired interval measures evaluation-unit variation only (add training-seed sd 0.001), the fold is exposed after many selections, and the public score of the corresponding fold-1-held-out student family was 0.6639 (P2) - local differences of +0.003 have not reliably transferred. ## 8. Serving Native Rust engine ([`native/src/rnn_fast.rs`](../../../../../native/src/rnn_fast.rs), int16 weight panels, AVX2, normalisation folded into the first layer, event features computed in the engine, state reset per sequence, deterministic). About 74 µs/row for width 256 on one core; about 33-37 min for the 39M-row test when run alone on the portal. A package is accepted only after Python 3.11 offline checks, ABI, reset/determinism and prediction agreement (corr ≥ 0.99998 with the GPU model). ## 9. Why the ceiling is where it is (new this session) ![ladder](plots/lookahead_ladder.png) With the same GRU and *future* rows visible the score is 0.666 (causal), 0.680 (2 rows ahead), 0.711 (8), 0.780 (32), 0.891 (128), 0.960 (512). The label is a smooth function of a long future path, so the causal model is a price-move **forecaster**; recipe knobs (chunk length, bootstrap, snapping columns, width, epochs) all moved the score by ≤ ±0.001-0.002. ## How good can distillation actually be here (short answer)

The +0.0008 is expected: a mean-of-teachers target is just a **conditional-mean** target, and a same-capacity student fit to it converges near the average single teacher. There are no logits to smooth, so classic "dark knowledge" gains don't exist in pure clipped-MSE regression. Only three mechanisms can break the plateau:

1. **Densify the supervision manifold** — the one principled route for a single model to *reach or exceed* a 2-model blend is more effective data (teacher pseudo-labels on the 39M test inputs + augmented paths), i.e. reduce the student's variance below the teachers' variance rather than imitating their mean.
2. **Fix alignment with the data-generating process** — label-lead timing, class-3 noise, step dispersion (worth +0.001–0.003 if the EDA signals are real).
3. **Learn from teacher errors, not outputs** — boosting; the only path that can explicitly *exceed* the 2-teacher blend (served as a 2nd tiny model, within the 2–3-model budget).

Statistics to respect: fold-1 paired eval sd 0.0018, seed sd 0.001 → every arm needs same-seed pairing and a class-3-conditional readout; ≥2–3 seeds per claim. All six below keep the current student recipe (warm start, AdamW 1e-4, one-cycle, 3 ep, batch 16, chunk 2000) unless stated, so each is a one-variable A/B.

---

### M1. Disagreement/noise-adaptive α (selective-sample KD)

1. **Mechanism:** where teachers agree, labels are reliable and the parent already fits them; where teachers disagree (exactly class 3, 69% of residual SS) the ensemble mean is the *denoised* label. Per-row α = σ²_e,row / (σ²_e,row + σ²_n,k), k = row class, α∈[0.5, 0.95]. σ²_e is teacher spread; σ²_n,k is estimated once from train as Var(y − ŷ̄^T | class k) − mean σ²_e,k, floored at 0.
2. **Loss/targets:** L = Σ w(row)·[α_row·MSE(ŷS, ŷ̄T) + (1−α_row)·MSE(ŷS, y)], w=|clip(y,2)|; plus 0.05·MSE(aux_var_head(h_t), σ_e,row), head dropped at serving (its role is forcing the state to encode row uncertainty). Schedule variants: 3 ep lr 1e-4 / 6 ep lr 7e-5 / 10 ep lr 5e-5 — soft targets are label-smoothing-like, so longer training is safer than on labels; verify against the epoch-3 memorization cliff via snapshot curves.
3. **Signal:** teacher outputs + teacher variance + disagreement weighting.
4. **Data:** existing train-split caches; rows without labels (test/non-eval-fold valid inputs) enter at α=1.
5. **Falsifier:** 2 paired same-seed runs (α=1.0 on all class-3 rows vs flat 0.7). Look first at class-3-conditional WP; expect +0.0005–0.0015.
6. **Literature:** You et al. 2017 selective-sample ensemble compression ("Learning to Ensemble"); Li et al. 2017 "Learning from Noisy Labels with Distillation".

### M2. Cross-fit residual boosting (2nd-stage corrector)

1. **Mechanism:** train a fresh small GRU to predict the teacher ensemble's *error*, using its state to track the per-run level offset that head-only KD cannot express (94% of residual SS). Distinct from E-093 (GBM on row features): the offset lives in run identity/state, so a recurrent residual model is not a repeat of that failure.
2. **Loss/targets:** stage-2 target r = clip(y,±2) − clip(ŷ̄^T,±2) on train rows with **cross-fit** teachers (hold out 10% of train sequences to fit stage-2 and the blend coefficient λ honestly); L2 = Σ w·MSE(ŷ², r), GRU h=128, dropout 0.2, Muon-AdamW lr 5e-4, one-cycle, ≤3 ep, weight decay 0.02. Served: ŷ = ŷ¹ + λŷ² (2-model stack, h128 is cheaper than h256).
3. **Signal:** residual-of-teachers.
4. **Data:** train-split labels + caches only.
5. **Falsifier:** pre-check with no serving cost — train-split residual R²; kill if <0.02; then inner-split val R² must be ≥0.5× train R². Highest-variance arm: +0.001–0.003 if the offset is causally predictable, ≈0 if it is future information.
6. **Literature:** Friedman 2001 gradient boosting; Cortes, Mohri & Syed 2014 deep boosting.

### M3. Lead-corrected targets (anticipation distillation) — the unconventional one

1. **Mechanism:** the label steps ~1 row before features do. Distill targets advanced one row, ṽ(t) = ŷ^T(t+1), so the teacher's own lagged response becomes the student's *anticipation*: the student learns to fire the step from pre-event cues (trade flow, book imbalance) instead of reacting to the already-moved book. On non-step rows ŷ(t+1)≈ŷ(t), so it is harmless where no timing bias exists. Step rows carry the heavy |clip(y,2)| metric weights, so timing errors are expensive exactly where they occur.
2. **Loss/targets:** L = 0.6·w·MSE(ŷS(t), ŷ^T(t+1)) + 0.4·w·MSE(ŷS(t), y(t)); otherwise identical student schedule (3 ep / 1e-4, sweep 6 ep / 7e-5).
3. **Signal:** teacher outputs, time-shifted.
4. **Data:** existing caches — no teacher re-runs.
5. **Falsifier (free, ~30 min, CPU):** compute pooled WP of ŷ^T(t+k) vs y(t) for k∈{−2..+2} on train rows; if the best shift is k=0, kill without any fit. If k=+1 wins, the gain is directly quantified before spending GPU.
6. **Literature:** no direct distillation paper known to me; closest analogues are TD/lookahead targets (Sutton & Barto, ch. 6–7) and lead-lag estimation via cross-correlation.

### M4. Augmented-path + transductive pseudo-label distillation

1. **Mechanism:** teachers are frozen and causal, so they can be re-run on *modified streams* to create supervision the student never sees in raw data: (a) random time-warp (segment-wise stretch/compress 0.8–1.25×; labels are step-interpolated harmlessly, but we use teacher outputs only); (b) rate dilution (drop 12%/15%-clock updates to simulate slow regimes); (c) Gaussian noise on quantile-transformed inputs with the teacher as denoiser. This distills the teacher *function*, not its values on train points — the standard capacity-mitigation when student ≈ teacher size. Optionally add teacher pseudo-labels on test/non-eval-fold-valid **inputs** (39M rows; pure KD needs no labels).
2. **Loss/targets:** augmented rows get pure-KD loss w_aug·MSE(ŷS, ŷ^T) with w_aug=|clip(ŷ^T,2)|; each epoch = 1 pass real train rows (current blend loss) + 1 pass over ~30–50% as many augmented/pseudo rows. Same student schedule; one-code A/B vs no-augmentation, same seed.
3. **Signal:** teacher outputs on OOD paths.
4. **Data:** warped/diluted train streams + (validity permitting; keep eval-fold inputs out) pseudo-labeled test/valid inputs. Record transductivity — using eval-fold inputs inflates the local number.
5. **Falsifier:** 1-epoch screen on a fixed augmented pool; kill if ΔWP ≤ 0 in the paired run. Expect +0.001–0.002.
6. **Literature:** Furlanello et al. 2018 Born-Again Networks; Yin et al. 2020 "Dreaming to Distill" (DeepInversion, data-free KD); time-warping surveyed in Iwana & Uchida 2021.

### M5. Multi-quantile predictive-distribution distillation

1. **Mechanism:** the student under-disperses the t0/t1 difference and step magnitudes; matching only the mean cements that. Instead make the student output τ-quantiles of the *ensemble's* predictive distribution (τ grid {0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95} per target = 10 head columns; serve the medians, same per-row cost, int8-safe). Pinball losses at multiple τ force the correct spread automatically and fix under-dispersion where the metric weights |y| heavy.
2. **Loss/targets:** L = Σ_τ pinball_τ(ŷS_τ, ŷ̄^T) with w=|clip(y,2)|, plus 0.2·Σ_τ pinball_τ(ŷS_τ, y) for calibration; schedule as in M1.
3. **Signal:** rank/quantile targets (full predictive distribution).
4. **Data:** existing caches.
5. **Falsifier:** pre-check from saved predictions — compare pooled and per-class std of current student vs ensemble; if within ~1–2%, the mechanism has no headroom and dies for free. Otherwise paired same-seed run; expect +0.0005–0.002.
6. **Literature:** Koenker & Bassett 1978 quantile regression; distribution-matching KD variants (moment/pinball matching).

### M6. Hidden-trajectory distillation from a wider teacher

1. **Mechanism:** the per-run level offset must live in the recurrent *state*, and head-only KD transfers the read-out, not the state geometry. Take an h384 (or 3-layer) teacher, project its per-row hidden states with trainable linear adaptors P_l (384→256) and require the student's states to match. Supervision is 20,000 rows/sequence vs 2 outputs — dense, and exactly where the 94%-offset residual lives.
2. **Loss/targets:** L = output KD + β·Σ_l mean_rows MSE(P_l h^T_t, h^S_t), β∈{0.1, 0.5}; P training-time only — served student is unchanged h256, fully deterministic.
3. **Signal:** hidden states.
4. **Data:** train split; teacher forward pass cached.
5. **Falsifier:** same-seed pair with/without hint loss, 2 seeds, β grid; kill if paired mean Δ ≤ +0.0003. Expect +0.0005–0.001 (this is the queued "hidden-state matching" arm).
6. **Literature:** Romero et al. 2015 FitNets; Zagoruyko & Komodakis 2017 attention transfer.

---

### Suggested order

M3's offline shift check (free) → M1+M5 as one 2×2 factorial (target-only changes, 8 short student runs, class-3-conditional readout) → M6 (queued) → M2 (upside arm, needs the honest inner-split λ) → M4 (most compute; the only arm aimed at beating the blend with a single model). M1/M2/M4 are pairwise compatible and likely additive: adaptive α decides *where* to listen, M4 *densifies* what it listens to, M2 corrects *what is left*.

I'd not re-run: mean-teacher temperature (MSE-equivalent), correlation loss (HPO null), EMA/SWA/chrono (tested negative), per-sequence adaptive ensemble weights (tested negative) — the six above are mechanistically none of these.
